events.title: THE HOUSEHOLD INSPECTIONS REACH THE OUTER STORAGE AND FIELD BOUNDARIES
events.body: The household's established inspections continue into the outer storage areas and the newly incorporated field boundaries. The men check gates, stores, tools, and boundary points while the stewards compare what they find with the estate's ordinary records. No seizure or confrontation accompanies the inspection, and local workers encountered during the rounds are addressed according to Valerius's renewed instructions on respectful conduct. A discrepancy in the placement of two agricultural tools is corrected in the household inventory before the day's work closes. The inspection produces another small addition to the estate's administrative record without changing the household's military posture.

events.title: A MARCELLUS LETTER SEEKS CLARIFICATION ON ONE ENTRY IN THE RAID DOSSIER
events.body: A letter associated with Marcus Claudius Marcellus reaches the estate with a request for clarification concerning one dated entry in the preserved raid dossier. The question concerns the distinction between an original observation and a later report copied into the chronology. Valerius's scribes locate the corresponding papers and prepare a written clarification that preserves the distinction rather than silently rewriting the record. The response identifies the source and date of the disputed entry and refers the Roman correspondent back to the authenticated copy already held in the archive. The exchange adds another layer of documentary precision to an inquiry that remains open.

events.title: TWO NEIGHBORING WORKERS ASK TO CONTINUE USING THE ESTATE'S SHARED WATERING ROUTE
events.body: Two neighboring agricultural workers approach the estate stewards with a practical request concerning a watering route that crosses the edge of the recently purchased tract. They explain that the route has been used during the spring season before the purchase and ask that ordinary access continue while the fields are being worked. The stewards bring the matter to Valerius rather than answering by force, and the existing route is temporarily recognized for ordinary agricultural use while its exact boundaries are entered into the property notes. The arrangement avoids a fresh dispute at a time when the surrounding fields are already under pressure from seasonal labor demands. The neighboring workers leave with the understanding that the arrangement is administrative and does not alter ownership.

events.title: THE PURCHASED FIELDS COMPLETE THEIR FIRST FULL SPRING WORK CYCLE
events.body: The newly purchased fields complete their first full cycle of spring preparation under the estate's administration. Workers finish the remaining preparation and begin the next stage of cultivation while the stewards track labor and stores separately from the older fields. Grain and fodder reserves are drawn down again to support the expanded work, but the household's organization allows the additional acreage to be handled without disrupting the established estate schedule. Several local workers who have been participating in the seasonal work receive their ordinary provisions and continue into the next stage. The tract is now functioning as part of the productive estate while its original purchase records remain preserved in the property archive.

events.title: THE LAKE-PORT MERCHANTS CONFIRM AN EARLY SPRING DELIVERY WINDOW
events.body: Word returns from the lake-port that merchants are prepared to receive an early spring delivery from the estate's stores. The arrangement is modest and concerns ordinary agricultural produce rather than an exceptional commercial venture, but the warehouse workers begin preparing the necessary space and measures. Valerius's administrators review the terms before allowing the goods to be moved, keeping the transaction separate from the household's military and political correspondence. The confirmation gives the estate a practical outlet for part of its spring production while maintaining the merchant relationships already established around the lake-port. The first loads are scheduled for the following period after the household completes its final measures.

events.title: THE WEEK'S ESTATE ACCOUNTS CLOSE WITH ORDINARY RECEIPTS AND HOUSEHOLD COSTS
events.body: At the close of the week, the estate stewards reconcile the ordinary books against the field work, storage preparations, and commercial commitments recorded during the preceding days. A small realized receipt is entered for produce already sold or contracted under the estate's ordinary spring activity, while the week's labor, provisions, maintenance, and administrative costs are recorded separately. The household's accounts distinguish the realized public operating profit from the established private transfer rather than treating the transfer as new income. The books are copied into the household records and the supporting commercial entries are retained for later comparison with the lake-port settlement. No investment return is entered because no established rate or maturity record supports one.
